o1.biggest_strength: It singles out the Essentials 8+ leak with real numbers (about 29% of churned revenue, 73% of exits tied to cost or approvals), and its test uses a control group and clear go and stop thresholds on switch rate, churn and Team downgrades.
o1.biggest_mistake: The base case is optimistic (half of the 8+ group switching, churn falling to 5%), and the yearly-billing fix, which is the faster win, gets only one line instead of a proper role.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make a yearly-billing nudge an explicit early move that helps the board window, and make the base case more cautious so the downside is not so far from it.
o1.vs_note: Customer email and public post are in the brand voice, with no urgency and the customer's own bill shown beside the new price.

o2.biggest_strength: It is honest about the downside (a low case of -$104k), adds a quick data check on single-user Team accounts before anything launches, and includes a clear pricing page table and dated plan.
o2.biggest_mistake: It waves away yearly billing as a "runner-up" that misses the board window, which overlooks the 0.9% vs 4.0% churn signal, and it adds a second option to a brief that asked for one recommendation.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Fold a yearly-billing offer into the single recommendation, and test the churn effect on existing 8+ customers rather than only measuring 60-day revenue from new visitors.
o2.vs_note: The new-visitor test has a small sample and a short window, so it cannot show whether churn improves, which is the main source of the gain.

reason: Owner would rather have the plan whose test directly checks the churn and downgrade assumptions with a control group, and which at least offers yearly billing at the switch. The other has a sharp data check and honest cases but dismisses the yearly lever and tests mostly new visitors.
